{"emailHash":"5ca94dfc0b92af595ae205d10c045a802f3e9d098ff657a20f5b3821d294f730","parentHash":null,"sequentialName":"Email 4088","from":"Raminder Grewal","to":"Natasha Geraldo Baird","subject":"Fw: Formal grievance","date":"2025-11-03T09:05:32.000Z","attachments":true,"body":"\r\n\r\nFYI.  I have forwarded to Heminsley for advice.  Sent from Outlook for iOS​​​​Raminder GrewalGlobal HR Director+44 (0) 7890 043 718From: Raminder Grewal <rgrewal@pogustgoodhead.com>Sent: Monday, November 3, 2025 9:02 amTo: Matt Hunt <mhunt@pogustgoodhead.com>Subject: Re: Formal grievance Dear Matt, I write to acknowledge receipt of your grievance. Thank you for setting out your concerns.  I'll be in touch very shortly to outline next steps as to your grievance and how we address the issues outlined. Rest assured, I'll prioritise the matter. Kind regards, Raminder ​Sent from Outlook for iOS​​​​Raminder GrewalGlobal HR Director+44 (0) 7890 043 718From: Matt Hunt <mhunt@pogustgoodhead.com>Sent: Sunday, November 2, 2025 4:16 pmTo: Raminder Grewal <rgrewal@pogustgoodhead.com>Subject: Formal grievance Dear Raminder,Please consider this a formal grievance in accordance with the firm's grievance policy (v1.0, 4 July 2024).Acas early reconciliation processThis is a unique grievance for two reasons.  First, the grievance is with senior leadership of the firm, whom I understand will have responsibility for considering whether to uphold or dismiss it.  Second, its subject matter has been repeatedly ignored or dismissed by that leadership.  I therefore do not believe that it will be dealt with properly, and as set out below believe the firm has no incentive to deal with it properly.The formal grievance process is therefore, in my view, not entirely adequate.  Accordingly, whilst I ask that you please treat this message as raising a formal grievance, please also consider it notification that I intend to contact Acas to engage the early reconciliation process.Adverse health effectsThe stress that I feel, and the mental health effects of PG's various reactions to the case leads' resignation, are documented in my resignation letter and various emails to the board (see, e.g., 3 October email from Michael Burke at 12:29, “we cannot stress enough how traumatic we and the entire team are finding this process, and that it is happening on the eve of trial”).   I have not received even a bare acknowledgement of my stress, let alone any sympathy or attempt to address my concerns.  Requests for explanations and information are consistently ignored (see, e.g., 9 October email from Michael Burke at 18:14).  Attempting to run the PDD Trial, whilst being repeatedly distracted by the firm's behaviour, is affecting my health.  A recent example is that, on 24 October 2025, the emissions "case leads" had a meeting at which quantum resourcing was discussed.  In response to the suggestion that Peter Gallagher be involved, rather than a reasoned explanation be given, Anna Varga shouted that "I [Anna] know you are all going to JLG."  The suggestion that I am motivated by some sort of conspiracy, rather than my clients' best interests, is insulting and has no basis in reality.Having reflected, I have spoken to a mental health nurse, using my health insurance provided by the firm, for advice on how to address this stress.  The nurse advised me immediately to self-certify as off work sick with stress, and seek an appointment with a doctor to see if more than a week off is appropriate. In any other circumstances I would do that, but at the moment I am torn as I care deeply about the trial and our clients.  The firm’s combination of silence and aggression leads me to infer that the firm, aware of my devotion to the trial, clients and colleagues, is anticipating that I will simply carry on regardless.  This inference only worsens my state.  Finally, whilst the firm needs me until the PCD section of the PDD Trial is complete on 28 November, from that point I believe that the firm will consider me dead weight.Requested resolutionPlease provide a proposal for the following:An acknowledgement of stress that the firm's treatment of the case leads has caused.An apology for the same.Compensation.The firm must have been aware of the health effects of its treatment of staff for a long time (my resignation letter explained my stress months ago), and so should be able to provide the above promptly.I look forward to hearing from you.Kind regards,Matt​​​​Matt Hunt(He/Him)Legal Director+44 (0) 7890 043 697"}

​​​​Raminder GrewalGlobal HR Director+44 (0) 7890 043 718From: Matt Hunt <mhunt@pogustgoodhead.com>Date: Friday, 14 November 2025 at 19:22To: Raminder Grewal <rgrewal@pogustgoodhead.com>Subject: Re: Formal grievanceDear Raminder,I am going to some time to consider your email, which is particularly demotivating to receive on the eve of the PCD section of trial.Matt​​​​Matt Hunt(He/Him)Legal Director+44 (0) 7890 043 697From: Raminder Grewal <rgrewal@pogustgoodhead.com>Sent: Friday, November 14, 2025 17:25To: Matt Hunt <mhunt@pogustgoodhead.com>Subject: Re: Formal grievance Dear Matt,Thank you for attending the grievance meeting on 7 November 2025 and for setting out your concerns in writing. Georgina Fallows accompanied you to the meeting. I appreciate the demands of the ongoing PDD Trial and your willingness to engage in this process despite those pressures. My email confirms the outcome of the grievance process. 1. Summary of Your Grievance  Your grievance raised the following main issues:Stress and adverse health effects, which you attribute to actions or omissions of senior leadership following the case leads’ resignationsPerceived lack of acknowledgement or response to you and colleagues regarding various concerns raised in emailsConduct during the case-leads meeting on 24 October 2025, specifically a comment made by Anna Varga, Lead Emissions partner,  about the potential move of staff to JLGBroader concerns about senior leadership, culture, media activity, and the leak of the interim report, which you indicated contributed to embarrassment, stress and concerns about the firm’s governanceA request for remedies to include an acknowledgement of stress caused by the firm, an apology and compensationA request to leave immediately after the conclusion of the PCD phase of the trial (28 November 2025), rather than complete your contractual notice period ending 15 December 2025.2. Findings2.1 Responses to concerns raised by case leadsYou expressed frustration that your emails and those of colleagues did not receive the responses you expected. Having reviewed the relevant correspondence, I acknowledge that some responses were delayed or brief. Responses were provided on a number of occasions, although they did not always address every point raised in depth. It is clear that senior leadership have been operating under significant time pressure during an exceptionally active phase of litigation, which affected the level of detail they were able to provide. Having reviewed the correspondence, I have found no evidence that any delays or brevity in replies were intended to ignore or dismiss your concerns.2.2 Stress and adverse health effectsYou described experiencing stress and having sought advice from a mental health nurse, who recommended self-certification. You explained that you continued working due to your commitment to the trial and clients.The firm does take well-being seriously and your comment on the impact on you is noted. I have found no evidence that the firm engaged in conduct intended to cause you stress. The pressures you described appear to arise primarily from the ongoing challenges we face with our litigation and the organisational changes underway. While I recognise that you personally experienced stress, I have not found evidence of unreasonable treatment or any breach of duty by the firm. Whilst you confirmed in our meeting that you did not require any personal adjustments, you remain encouraged to use all available wellbeing resources, including visiting your doctor as advised by the medical nurse, as well as the employee assistance programme and your private medical insurance. If you wish to discuss any additional support we can offer you, I remain available to assist you.2.3 The 24 October meetingYou raised concerns regarding a comment made by Anna Varga, which you felt was factually wrong and unhelpful. In reviewing this matter,  my view is that the comment was made without the intention you inferred; however, I do fully accept that it did not reflect the facts, as it is correct that not all staff leaving the firm are moving to JLG and you are right to point this out. 2.4 Concerns regarding senior leadership, public communications, governance matters and disclosure of the interim reportYou raised several concerns relating to the wider conduct of senior leadership, including:Embarrassment caused by public statements or media exchanges involving the firm Alleged tensions or disputes between senior individualsThe governance structure of the firm and its alignment with litigation strategyThe leak of an interim report to the media.I fully acknowledge that these issues have caused you concern and that you perceive them as contributing to the pressures you have experienced and I also recognise that they may have affected the broader working environment for both you and your colleagues. However, after careful consideration, I must confirm that these matters relate to organisational governance, strategic communications and the conduct of senior individuals in their executive capacities and therefore do not relate specifically to your individual employment relationship or fall within the scope of the grievance procedure. In addition, several of the concerns you raised, particularly regarding the interim report leak and media activity, are already being considered through separate internal processes and cannot be managed through the grievance route. While I recognise that you understandably have strong views about these issues and feel they contributed to the stress you experienced, the evidence available does not indicate that they resulted in targeted or unreasonable treatment towards you as an individual.3. RemedyYou requested an acknowledgement that the firm caused you stress, an apology, and compensation. After considering all of the information available, I do not find that the firm’s actions constituted unreasonable treatment, misconduct, or a breach of duty. Accordingly, I cannot conclude that the firm was responsible for causing the stress you describe and an apology would therefore not be appropriate in circumstances where the grievance has not been upheld. For the same reason, compensation is not warranted. That said, I recognise the pressures you have been under and am sorry that you have experienced this period as distressing. Although this does not amount to an acceptance of fault, I do want to acknowledge the impact you described during our meeting.4. Request to Leave After the PCD PhaseDuring our meeting, you indicated a wish to conclude your employment after the PCD phase of the PDD Trial ends on 28 November 2025, rather than work until the end of your contractual notice period on 15 December 2025. I have discussed the matter with Anna Varga and unfortunately, we are unable to accommodate your request to leave earlier. A full and thorough handover is essential to ensure continuity and to meet our client obligations. Your continued availability is also necessary to support colleagues who will be assuming your responsibilities. For these reasons, you are required to work your full notice period, ending on 15 December 2025, in accordance with your employment contract. We will, of course, work with you to ensure that the handover process is structured, manageable and appropriately supported.5. Support Going ForwardI appreciate the candid and constructive manner in which you raised your concerns. I will continue to support you throughout the remainder of your notice period. Should you wish to discuss workload management, handover planning, or wellbeing resources, please let me know.6. Right of AppealYou are entitled to submit a written appeal within 10 working days of receiving this letter to @HR Team, setting out the grounds of your appeal.  Thank
